summary: @servicetitan/uikit-docs preinstall drops Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall="node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is an obfuscator.io-style script (_0xNNNN identifiers, string dictionaries) that, when Bun is not already installed on the host, downloads a Bun binary zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and execFileSyncs it against a sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB payload beginning with '// @bun @bun-cjs' and using a string-array rotator plus a custom base64-style decoder with a scrambled alphabet — a runtime string/code decoder that hides the payload's actual behavior from Node-based static analysis. The package's declared purpose is MDX documentation files, which do not require a second language runtime. The manifest declares "files": ["docs"], but the published tarball also contains root-level setup.mjs and math_init.js — both fall outside the declared file allowlist, consistent with files injected outside the normal publish flow. The Bun runtime install is the mechanism, not the attack: the attack is that Bun is used to execute an obfuscated, undeclared, purpose-mismatched local payload at npm install time, bypassing Node-resolved static analysis of what actually runs on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
